text:
maria.chen: Quick callout from the quant follow-up meeting: we need a tiny, standardized handshake between the runtime and infra that conveys the chosen precision profile + an easy-to-parse quality signal for routing/fallback decisions. I sketched a minimal header below.

maria.chen: sketch (minimal, machine-friendly):
```json
{
  "profile": "fp8-xgboost-style-v1",
  "profile_version": 1,
  "quality_delta_abs": 0.025,      // absolute delta on primary metric (e.g. perplexity or rougeL), lower is better
  "fallback": "int8-std-v3",
  "max_extra_latency_ms": 12,
  "canary_fraction": 0.05,
  "probe_ids": ["smoke-2026-03", "eval-rt1"]
}
```

devon: prefer quality_delta_abs to pct as well. For API clarity we should also include metric_name (e.g. "perplexity" or "rougeL") so infra knows how to interpret the number across endpoints.

nina: telemetry: emit quant.profile.apply, quant.profile.fallback, quant.profile.estimate. Fields: req_id, model, model_version, profile, profile_version, sample_id, metric_name, quality_delta_abs, tokens_in/tokens_out, latency_ms, region, canary_id (if any).

samir: also call out cost impact estimate. If fp8 reduces cost by 30% but increases tail-degradation risk, infra might choose to cap concurrency differently. Add optional field cost_savings_pct.

pranay: operational piece: canary behavior should be explicit in the header but enforced by infra. I recommend: canary_fraction + canary_duration_min + auto_rollback_threshold (on quality_delta_abs or sample failure rate). Example: auto_rollback_threshold=0.05.

maria.chen: updated minimal header suggestion with metric_name + cost_savings_pct. Keep runtime surface minimal (runtime only needs to return the profile used and observed degradation).

devon: proto nit: name the header QuantProfileHint and keep unknown fields ignored for forward-compat. We'll include profile_key, profile_v, metric_name, numeric_delta, fallback_key, ops_tags.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary cny-900 launched for fp8-xgboost-style-v1 -> 5% traffic us-west2. Link: https://deploys/internal/cny-900

nina: add a tiny probe harness: replay eval-rt1 snippets through canary pool every 10 minutes and emit quant.profile.estimate events to the eval topic. That should let infra compute real-time drift.

samir: note re: fallback pools 0% of fallback capacity should be in different AZs when max_extra_latency_ms < 20ms to avoid correlated SLO hits. Put this rule in the ops checklist.

pranay: I'll write the canary playbook: step-by-step (start canary -> run probes -> wait grace_period_min -> assess metrics -> auto rollback if > threshold). Will include alerting thresholds and paging playbook.

maria.chen: We also discussed a tiny runtime shim that only emits: {observed_profile, observed_metric_name, observed_delta, observed_latency_ms, sample_count} back to the control plane. Runtime shouldn't do routing. Keep it stateless.

devon: I'll PR a proto + small runtime shim interface that reads QuantProfileHint and emits QuantProfileTelemetry. I'll add a compatibility test that verifies unknown keys are ignored.

nina: I'll post the telemetry schema + example Grafana panels in #eng-infra.

samir: I'll estimate perf overhead of the shim (should be <1% p99 increase) and check memory for cached profile metadata.

maria.chen: Action list: devon proto + PR, nina telemetry + panels, pranay canary playbook + runbook link, samir perf/memo. I'll draft a 1-page RFC and include example JSONs + playbook. Thanks. :thumbsup:

pranay: quick Q: should probes be synchronous (block canary eval) or async? I suggest async to avoid latency amplification, but mark critical probes as sync during initial 10m.

devon: agree async by default, sync for the smoke QA subset. We'll make that configurable via probe_ids.

maria.chen: ok great. I'll publish the RFC tomorrow and add the sample proto in the doc.
